title: Taxes (Collection) Ordinance
source_id: חא״י כרך ב׳ פרק קל״ז, עמ׳ 1374; ע״ר 1937, תוס׳ 1, 104; ע״ר תש״ח, תוס׳ א׳, 1; Knesset legislation database lawitemid 2000886; Wikisource page פקודת המסים (גבייה)
verified_how: Fetched the Wikisource page. Heading prints פקודת המסים (גביה) with no Hebrew year; metadata gives חא״י כרך ב׳ פרק קל״ז, עמ׳ 1374, ע״ר 1937, תוס׳ 1, 104 and ע״ר תש״ח, תוס׳ א׳, 1, and Knesset lawitemid 2000886; most recent amendment noted תשפ״ב, 887 (2022) with a deferral notice at ק״ת תשפ״ג, 962. Section headings cover demand for payment, seizure of movable and immovable property, third-party garnishment, sale of seized property, and registration blocks, with modern amendments on electronic documents and service. No repeal notice appears on the page.
notes: MANDATE-ERA ORDINANCE (commonly cited as the Taxes (Collection) Ordinance 1929; the printed consolidated heading carries no year, and the citations on the page are to חא״י and to the 1937 and 5708 Official Gazette, so no year is asserted here). Included because it, not the Income Tax Ordinance, supplies the enforced-collection machinery - demand, seizure, garnishee, sale - for income tax and most other taxes, including recovery of amounts a withholding agent failed to deduct or remit. It is the instrument a taxpayer in default is actually governed by. It is Ordinance-form but heavily modernised; the ק״ת תשפ״ג, 962 entry indicates a deferral of commencement of part of the 2022 amendment, so check commencement before relying on the latest text.
